run.title: Run Ze on your Linux host.
run.label: Linux
run.body: Run Ze as a Linux service to use your host as a router or replace an existing ExaBGP setup. For migration, convert your configuration and use the compatibility bridge for process scripts, checking the documented differences before switching.
run.success: Check your sessions and routes. If migrating from ExaBGP, verify your process scripts before switching.

run.title: Run Ze in Docker.
run.label: Docker
run.body: Run Ze's routing daemon in a container, with persistent configuration and the host managing its network interfaces. Docker is also an option for replacing ExaBGP, using the same migration tools and compatibility bridge.
run.success: Check your sessions and routes, then verify that your configuration survives container recreation.

run.title: Give Ze its own system.
run.label: Appliance
run.body: Build a dedicated router on hardware or a VM with Ze's immutable operating system. Ze manages the network configuration, while the guide covers installation, authenticated SSH, updates and previous-slot recovery.
run.success: Source builds produce disk images and installer ISOs. No public image release is available yet.

run.title: Test a network topology.
run.label: Containerlab
run.body: Use netlab with containerlab to run Ze in a test network. Start with the supplied topology to explore routing and check how Ze behaves before using it in your own network.
run.success: Check BGP sessions, kernel routes and traffic between the lab nodes.

who.title: Lab router
who.label: Lab
who.body: Network builders can bring up two BGP peers, inspect routes, and check whether Ze's operator tools fit their workflow.

who.title: Test with an AI agent
who.label: AI agent
who.body: Use Claude Code or Codex to check a lab configuration and explore Ze's commands. ze create agent skill installs instructions that match your installed version.

link.label: Use Ze with an AI agent

who.title: ExaBGP replacement
who.label: Migration
who.body: ExaBGP users can try the migrator against an existing config and see which process scripts still translate cleanly.

who.title: White-box appliance
who.label: Appliance
who.body: People with spare x86 hardware can boot the appliance image and test the same configuration model without a general-purpose shell.

who.title: Looking glass
who.label: Operate
who.body: Operators who need read-only BGP visibility can publish a looking glass and inspect routes without giving shell access.

who.title: Protocol testbed
who.label: Interop
who.body: Protocol implementers can run Docker interop scenarios against FRR, BIRD, and GoBGP, then turn a failure into a test case.

who.title: AI-assisted operations
who.label: MCP
who.body: MCP exposes Ze commands and structured output to AI tools without a separate command set.
